> **In this skill:** a project folder stands in for `assets/`: `manifest.json` plus each spec it writes in `<kind>/specs/<id>.json`; the library in `references/library/` is the other spec root, and `scripts/compile.mjs` stands in for `scripts/build-solution.ts` and the checks. "Proven" refers to runs on the gallery repo's lab account. Links to other repo files are background reading the skill does not ship.

# Solution manifest: one file for every asset a solution needs

## Contents

- What the manifest says, and what it does not
- Keys
- The bundle
- Prerequisites (derived)
- Checking (`src/solution-check.ts`)
- Account values (`--account`)
- The three manifests
- Deploying a manifest
- Limits

A **solution manifest** (`assets/solutions/<id>.json`) names every asset one customer solution needs and the
decisions that tie them together. `scripts/build-solution.ts` compiles it offline into a **bundle**,
`dist/solutions/<id>.zip`: every uploadable file, a `README.md` with the upload order and the upload path per
file, and a `solution.json` with what the compile found. This is phase 2 of
[PROMPT-TO-ASSETS-PLAN.md](PROMPT-TO-ASSETS-PLAN.md). Each README upload line links to its section of [UPLOAD-GUIDES.md](UPLOAD-GUIDES.md): the click
path, what to pick, what to check and the common errors, with screens.

```
npx tsx scripts/build-solution.ts <id> …          # one or more manifests
npx tsx scripts/build-solution.ts --all
npx tsx scripts/build-solution.ts <id> --account=<values.json>   # built for one account (below)
```

The compiler is `src/solution-spec.ts`. Workflows go through `src/scenario-build.ts`, the same compile
`captures/deploy-scenario.ts` runs, so a bundle and a deploy built from the same account values hold the same
bytes (`test/solution-spec.test.ts`). The other kinds go through their own compilers. Every file is checked
against [docs/schemas/](schemas/) before the bundle is written; a failure stops the build.

## What the manifest says, and what it does not

The manifest holds only **decisions**. Everything a compiler can read off the specs is **derived** into the
bundle and never written twice:

| In the manifest (decided) | In the bundle (derived) |
|---|---|
| the assets, by library id or inline | what each workflow package carries: request types and their intake forms, web forms, document templates, eSignature templates, statuses |
| the import order of the workflows | the Salesforce objects and fields the reads and templates use |
| which request types the workflows share | the account custom fields an import creates or updates (hard to undo) |
| a carried template's own name; templates named instead of carried | the connected apps (an `ACT` component: Salesforce) |
| prerequisites no spec shows | the preflight of `src/deploy-preflight.ts`, statuses created vs reused, the 30-status cap |

## Keys

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | kebab-case | the file name and the bundle's name |
| `name`, `description` | string | the README's title and first paragraph |
| `namePrefix` | string | starts every created name (`ZZ Lab · ` in the lab). Agents take it without punctuation (`ZZ Lab `: the agent name rule allows letters, numbers and spaces). CLM workflows take `CLM_PREFIX` instead (`ZZ Lab - `; CLM names allow no `·`). |
| `environment` | `demo` \| `production` | Send an Email's service host. Default `demo` |
| `agents` | refs | Agent Studio agents. A workflow names an agent by key and never carries it, so every agent a workflow runs must be listed; the compiler refuses one that is not. |
| `workflows` | refs | Workflow Builder workflows, **in import order** |
| `sharedRequestTypes` | request-type ids | types several workflows use: the FIRST workflow whose Create a Request opens one carries it (else the first that starts on it); every later workflow names it. A Create a Request cannot name an existing type (the importer drops it), and a request start matches its type by name. |
| `templateNames` | spec id → name | a carried document template's name, when it differs from its spec's |
| `namedTemplates` | template spec ids | templates the workflows name instead of carrying. Their ids are the account's, so they need `--account` values. Carrying is the default: an import that only named a Salesforce template failed (500 ERR_10999, 2026-10-27). |
| `requestTypes`, `webforms`, `documentTemplates` | refs | assets uploaded on their own, not carried by a workflow |
| `esignTemplates` | library ids, or `{ id, set }` | standalone eSignature templates: a library id, or the project's own `esign-templates/specs/<id>.json` (`from` a library document template or an inline document), with its PDFs in `esign-templates/documents/`: printed by `npx tsx captures/esign-template-docs.ts <id> --root <project>` and committed with the manifest, or, in the skills, printed by `compile.mjs` with headless Chrome (`src/esign-template-print.ts`; same tabs, test/esign-template-print.test.ts). `set` gives a library template proven settings of its own (`reminders`, `expiration`, `carbonCopies`, `brand`): the same documents, rebuilt. |
| `clmWorkflows` | refs | CLM Advanced Workflows ([CLM-WORKFLOW-SPEC.md](CLM-WORKFLOW-SPEC.md)) |
| `clmDocgenForms` | refs | CLM Document Generation forms (`assets/clm-docgen-forms/specs/`, `src/clm-docgen-form.ts`). Not an upload: the bundle carries the form's configuration (`.clm-form.json`) and a build sheet with the merge tags; `deploy-scenario --solution` saves it as the form editor does (`captures/lib-clm-docgen.ts`), named `<CLM prefix><name>`; park it by hand. A form with `template` also carries its Word template (`.docx`) |
| `clmDocgenConfigs` | `[{ form, name?, launch?, folder: { path, name?, uid? } }]` | CLM doc-gen CONFIGURATIONS: a `clmDocgenForms` form with a `template`, its Word template, the destination folder and the CLM workflow it launches (published first). Give `launch`: a configuration with none opens as "Invalid Document Generation configuration" [observed 2026-10-31], so the bundle warns. The bundle carries a build sheet; `deploy-scenario --solution` uploads the `.docx` into the folder and saves the configuration (`src/clm-docgen-config.ts`, the body `captures/clm-docgen-config-verify.ts` proved); `folder.uid` is the account's and needed only to deploy |
| `clmEforms` | refs | CLM classic eForms (`assets/clm-eforms/specs/`, `src/clm-eform-spec.ts`): an intake or task form whose answers become attributes on a `.sxform` document (searchable, routable) or custom form answers. Not an upload and not deployed: the bundle carries the HTML to paste (`eforms/<id>.html`) and its steps (`eforms/<id>.md`: Create, paste, Save, Set Submit Folder, Set Workflow, Allow Submission). A spec's `workflow` may name one of this manifest's `clmWorkflows`. Attribute field ids come from the spec's `attributeIds` or the account values' `clmAttributeIds`; else the HTML holds `REPLACE:<Group.Field>` placeholders and a compile warning says so |
| `webformTemplates` | refs | template-linked web forms (`assets/webform-templates/specs/`, `src/webform-template-spec.ts`): a form built FROM a library eSignature template, whose last page signs it. Not an upload: the bundle carries the template's JSON, the form spec and a build sheet; `deploy-scenario --solution` builds it by API |
| `deskSettings` | refs | account-wide Agreement Desk settings (`assets/desk-settings/specs/`, `src/desk-settings.ts`): default type and status, Agreement Desk AI, email intake, notifications, the approvals block on Send for Signature. Not an upload: the bundle carries the spec (`<id>.desk-settings.json`) and a sheet of Requests ▸ Settings steps; `captures/desk-settings.ts --apply` sets and reads them back. It changes the whole account's desk, so pair it with a prerequisite question |
| `prerequisites` | strings | what the account must hold that no file creates and no spec shows. Each becomes a prerequisite line. |
| `integration` | strings | what a caller must send that the compile cannot see (a CSV header, a Flow's inputs). Each API-started workflow's trigger call and an example `trigger_inputs` payload are derived and printed anyway (README "Integration notes") |
| `notBuildable` | string | why nothing is built as asked; required when the bundle has no assets |
| `gaps` | `[{ need, capability?, instead? }]` | what the customer asked for that no compiler builds: the need in their words, the `docs/capabilities.json` id, and what the bundle does instead. The check refuses a gap whose capability is unknown or `proven` (build it instead), and warns on `compiled-unproven`. The README lists them under "Not built"; a gap whose `instead` starts with "built" ("built: …", a `compiled-unproven` setting that was used) is listed under "Built, not yet proven live" instead, beside every capability the bundle's specs use that is `compiled-unproven` (one line each, with the asset; the check's warning names the same ones). The check warns when a step's wording states a not-built gap as done. |

A **ref** is a library spec id (`"third-party-paper-triage"`) or an inline spec: `{ "id": "my-triage", "spec": { … } }`.
An inline id must not be a library id. An inline workflow may use inline request types, web forms, templates and
agents of the same manifest. Unknown keys are refused.

## The bundle

`<id>/README.md`, `<id>/solution.json`, and one file per upload step, numbered in upload order:

| Order | File | Upload path |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `NN-agent-<id>.md` (build sheet) + `NN-agent-<id>.revision.json` | Agent Studio ▸ Create agent, from the build sheet; publish. Or create it by API from the revision under its key (`captures/deploy-scenario.ts` does this): only then does the key match the one the workflow names. Agents have no import file. |
| 2 | `NN-request-type-<id>.zip` | Requests ▸ Settings ▸ Request types ▸ Import |
| 3 | `NN-webform-<id>.json` | Start ▸ Web Forms ▸ Upload Configuration, then activate |
| 4 | `NN-document-template-<id>.zip` | Templates ▸ Document Templates ▸ + Create New ▸ Upload (lands as a draft) |
| 5 | `NN-esign-template-<id>.json` | Templates ▸ Start ▸ Envelope Templates ▸ Upload Template |
| 6 | `NN-workflow-<name>.zip` | Agreements ▸ Workflows ▸ Create Workflow ▸ Import Workflow (lands as a draft) |
| 6b | `NN-webform-template-<id>.esign-template.json` + `.md` (build sheet) + `.form-spec.json` | NOT an upload: Upload Template the eSignature template, then Web Forms ▸ Create ▸ Transform a template and follow the build sheet; or `deploy-scenario --solution` (POST the form from the template, PATCH its content, activate) |
| 7 | `NN-clm-workflow-<id>.json` | CLM ▸ Workflows ▸ New Workflow ▸ Advanced Workflow ▸ start without content ▸ toolbar **Import** ▸ Save. Not Admin ▸ Workflows ▸ Download Workflow (download only), not Admin ▸ Deployment (a signed `.spackage`). |

The README gives, per step: the file, the upload path, what the import creates (request types, forms,
templates, statuses, custom fields), what it needs first (a shared type an earlier import made, an agent, a
connected app), and what to do after (point the Salesforce launcher or Flow at the new workflow). Above the
steps it lists every **prerequisite**, each with how to check it. Every README has **Test copies** (a name prefix
rebuild, or what can be renamed after an import, and for a Salesforce launcher start that the copy is its own menu item)
and, per workflow, **Running it**: how a run starts (a Salesforce launcher start is Start with Docusign on the record,
never an API call; an API start is the call under Integration notes) and who does what.

## Prerequisites (derived)

Each one is read off the assets, never written into the manifest. The account and org needs come from
`src/deploy-preflight.ts` (one row per need: what, how to check it, and the `docs/capabilities.json` rows it
stands for, which cover every row of `docs/capabilities.json` whose fix is "prerequisite" (the test holds them to it)); the rest from the
compile:

| When the bundle has | Prerequisites |
|---|---|
| any workflow | IAM plan; publish after import; a free published-workflow slot per workflow (COUNTED) |
| an Event start | Docusign Connect (a request start does not need it: Test 1, 2026-11-02) |
| a request start or Create a Request | app access (Agreement Desk); Agreement Desk set up (Requests ▸ Get Started, COUNTED); a request start with a step that changes the request: its publisher can manage all requests (COUNTED) |
| a send | no required envelope custom field; in-session signing for a direct send |
| an agent | create it first; a plan with Agent Studio; agent quota of 100 (COUNTED); AI controls; region and language; app access |
| a Salesforce read, start or template | app installed and connected (COUNTED); link health; org settings; the objects and fields the reads and templates use |
| a Salesforce launcher start | IAM for Sales and a shared connection; the user permission; the launcher component; add to the menu after publish |
| a Salesforce Flow start | the Flow names the new workflow id |
| statuses it creates | room under the 30-live-status cap |
| another connected app | installed and connected before import |
| an agent that searches agreements | the Agreement Manager portfolio it reads (and the 1,500-documents-per-seat allowance) |
| a CLM workflow | CLM on the account, Advanced Workflow rights; publish after Save under a unique name |

The README prints each one for the customer: what the account needs, how to check it in their own account, and the
Docusign help topic as a link — no repo paths. COUNTED (in solution.json) marks the ones `captures/deploy-scenario.ts`
also reads at deploy, read-only (published workflows, Salesforce connections, agents). A placeholder address
(`<role>@example.com`) gets one line listing every workflow step and field it sits in, derived from the compiled packages.

## Checking (`src/solution-check.ts`)

`checkSolution` runs every offline check in one pass: the compile (every compiler's refusals, every file's
schema), each workflow's required drawer fields and export-key parity, the help guidance (warnings), the
gap check, and every document template's `examples` (at least one; each gives every required sender field a value, a
listed option for a dropdown and rows for each line-item table: the generate gate runs it). `compileSolution(manifest, values, { roots })` takes spec roots: folders of `<kind>/specs/<id>.json`
(default: this repo's `assets/`); an id in two roots is refused. The corpus eval
(`npx tsx scripts/eval-corpus.ts`, [assets/prompt-corpus/expected/](../assets/prompt-corpus/expected/README.md))
and the `docusign-solution` skill both use it. How a prompt becomes a manifest: [SOLUTION-PLANNING.md](SOLUTION-PLANNING.md).

`solution.json` is the resolved manifest: the upload order with each file's sha256, each workflow's carried
and named components, statuses, Salesforce fields, connected apps, custom fields, the prerequisites and the gaps.

## Account values (`--account`)

Without them a bundle is **portable**:
- an agent's key is the one its `.revision.json` creates (`<prefix>_<name>_0`);
- every status is created under the prefix (`ZZ Lab · Pending Approval`);
- the shared types need no ids: a request-started package names a type by name only, so the
  placeholders build the same bytes as the real ids (checked in the test).

A JSON file of `AccountValues` (`src/solution-spec.ts`) builds for one account:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `agentKeys` | agent spec id → the key it has on the account |
| `statuses` | live status name → id. A package carrying a live status by its own id reuses it; nothing is created. |
| `templates` | `namedTemplates` spec id → `{ templateId, documentId, version }` |
| `owner` | the package owner `{ userId, userName }` |
| `directory` | account users and groups, for a workflow that names them. Without it each `{ "user" }` / `{ "group" }` compiles to a placeholder and the README says to pick the real one in each step it lists. |
| `clmUsers` | CLM user email → GUID, for a CLM step that names a user. Without `clmUsers` the bundle compiles each `{ "user" }` assignee empty and the README names the step to pick the user in after Import. |
| `clmAttributeIds` | CLM attribute `Group.Field` → field id, for the eForms. |
| `clmFolders` | CLM folder name → uid, for a step's `folder: { "name" }`. Without it the folder compiles empty and the README names the step to pick it in after Import. |
| `clmTaskGroups` | CLM task group name → uid, for a task's `assignee: { "taskGroup" }`. Without it the group compiles empty and the README names the step to pick it in after Import. |
| `salt`, `statusNameSuffix` | as the deploy uses them: fresh status and type ids for a re-import (a deleted one keeps its id and name for good) |

Every id is read from the account, never written to pass a compile (acceptance 4, bug 8). The compile refuses a made-up
one (`src/made-up-id.ts`): a GUID with a group of 8 or 12 that is one repeated character (`00000000-…`,
`…-111111111111`) or counts up (`12345678-…`), an id that says it is a stand-in (`placeholder…`, `replace…`,
`your-…`, `xxx`, `<…>`), and a directory user at `@example.com`. No corpus example ships an `account.json`.

## The three manifests

| Manifest | Stands for | Bundle |
|---|---|---|
| `sales-contract-approvals` | scenario (a2), [DEMO-SCENARIOS.md](DEMO-SCENARIOS.md) | 3 workflow packages: W1 carries `Sales Contract Request`, W1F carries `Sales Contract Request from Salesforce`, W2 names both and carries the order form as `Order Form (Salesforce) · Sales Contract` |
| `inbound-paper-triage` | scenario (b) | the triage agent's build sheet + revision, then the workflow carrying `Third-Party Paper Review` |
| `clm-msa-negotiation` | the CLM negotiation demo | the Import JSON of `msa-negotiation-external-review`, with the folder, document and contact as prerequisites |

`test/solution-spec.test.ts` holds them to the deploy: `planOf(manifest)` equals the `SCENARIOS` entry of
`src/scenario-build.ts`, and from the same account values every workflow package of the bundle hash-equals the
one `buildScenario` compiles for `captures/deploy-scenario.ts`. The CLM file equals `compileClmWorkflow`'s
output (what `captures/clm-workflow-verify.ts` imports, there under a `ZZ Lab - ` name).

## Deploying a manifest

`DS_ACCOUNT=default npx tsx captures/deploy-scenario.ts --solution=<id|manifest.json> [--publish] [--dry]` runs the same
deploy as `--scenario=`, with the manifest's plan (`deployablePlan`). It deploys:
- agents, workflows, template-linked web forms, CLM workflows and CLM doc-gen forms and configurations, by library id;
- library eSignature templates (`esignTemplates` by id, created by `POST /templates`) and, for one with a `salesforce`
  block, its eSignature for Salesforce envelope template: the `dfsle` records inserted in the connected org through the
  Salesforce host profile (`src/salesforce-rest.ts`), ledgered and parked by id (proven 2026-10-30, `mutual-nda-salesforce`);
- a workflow whose event start names one of those templates (`when.template { esign }`) is rebuilt with the template's new id
  after it is created, and refused if the template is not in `esignTemplates` (compiled, not yet proven live);
- under the prefix (`ZZ Lab · `; CLM: `ZZ Lab - `), ledgered under the manifest's id (park with `park-scenario.ts --scenario=<id>`).

It refuses another `namePrefix`, and specs with no legacy proof (the library's freshness check), unless it is a LAB
deploy: `DEPLOY_LAB=1` takes a corpus or project manifest with its own specs beside it, names everything `ZZ Lab …`,
and may target either account. `--skip-standalone` leaves the standalone uploads (document and eSignature templates,
request types, web forms) to their verifiers; without it, request types, web forms, document templates and an
eSignature template with its own `set` are refused (upload those from the bundle). Placeholders are swapped at deploy with `--user-alias`, `--group-alias`,
`--email-alias` (lab inboxes only) and `--clm-folder`. The phase 5 live sample deployed, published, ran and parked 10
corpus bundles this way: [LIVE-SAMPLE.md](LIVE-SAMPLE.md).

## Limits

- A bundle is compiled and checked offline. 10 corpus bundles have also been deployed, published and run live on both
  accounts ([LIVE-SAMPLE.md](LIVE-SAMPLE.md)); every other bundle is proven only by its specs' own proofs.
- An agent created by hand gets a key of its own: pick it again in each Execute AI Agent step after the import.
- An eSignature template written inline in the manifest is refused: give it a spec file in the project, with its printed PDFs.
- Imported workflows land as drafts; publishing (consent, the AI agent disclaimer) stays a person's step.
- Every send step of a bundle is compiled as "Automatically, by the creator": a hand import needs the roles re-picked,
  and the drawer keeps only that shape. A deploy with `deploy-scenario` keeps a send left as a draft for the starter.
- The upload order follows the dependencies: agents first, then standalone templates, forms and request types, then the
  workflows (each after what it names), CLM workflows before the doc-gen configurations that launch them. An eSignature
  template a workflow carries is not listed again as its own upload.
